title: credential-telemetry-decomposition-field-notes
content:
Context:
Quick field notes from an ad-hoc design session and backlog grooming for a per-credential / per-route telemetry page that helps SREs and customers debug quota/rate-limit behavior and attribute cost/latency back to credentials and routes. This is intentionally rough — meant to capture interaction ideas, edge cases, and implementation tradeoffs for the backlog grooming ticket.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Enable a user to answer: which credentials or routes caused throttling this week; which keys are driving the highest token spend; are latency regressions correlated with a particular credential, route, or model variant.
- Provide an efficient drilldown from high-level signals into sampled request traces (so teams can repro and triage).
- Keep the primary console latency low (few queries to backend) while supporting heavy aggregation and combinatorial filters.

Primary concepts / new vocabulary:
- Credential fingerprint: compact, stable label for a credential grouping that includes owner, project, and first-seen date. Use for rollup rows.
- Sparse journey: a low-cardinality visualization that shows representative request paths for a credential (e.g., typical route sequence + average tokens/latency). Helpful for quick triage without pouring through raw logs.
- Attribution slices: precomputed dimensions (token-count, request-count, throttled-count, error-count) broken out by route/model/time window.

Suggested page scaffolding (top -> deep):
1) Header summary strip (single row): active-credential-count, total-requests (selected window), throttle-events, token-cost-estimate, median-latency. Quick date picker + topology selector (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) Top contributors panel (left): ranked list of top 20 credentials by token-cost. Each row shows small sparkline of token-usage and an overflow menu.
3) Route heatmap (center): matrix of credentials (rows) x routes (columns) with color intensity for token usage or throttle rate. Hover tooltip shows: last 24h counts, sample request id, top model used. Click cell = open credential-route timeline.
4) Sparse journeys (right): per-credential carousel of 3 representative request patterns (fast/common, slow, throttled). Each pattern shows sequence of routes, average tokens, and a tiny waterfall for token/time split.
5) Bottom: timeline + trace panel: time-series stacked area (tokens by credential or route) with overlay markers for quota changes, deployments, and throttle spikes; selecting window populates sampled traces table.

Interaction details / microcopy ideas:
- Row actions: pin credential (keep at top), inspect (open modal with identity & last 10 request samples), mute (exclude from default ranking), create alert (pre-populated with chosen metric).
- Heatmap cell click: contextual flyout with 3 tabs: Metrics (counts, p50/p95 latency, model mix), Samples (list of sample request ids with links to trace viewer), Config (credential metadata + associated rate limit/quota config).
- Sparse journey card CTA: "Open trace" and "Re-run sample in sandbox" (sandbox rerun uses a stored prompt with anonymization rules).
- Empty state copy for low-traffic orgs: "No credential-level telemetry yet. Enable request sampling in project settings or increase retention to see granular breakdowns."

Performance / implementation notes (engineering constraints):
- Backend pre-aggregation: compute hourly rollups for credential x route x model to avoid ad-hoc heavy scans. Keep a bloom-filter-like lightweight index to enumerate active credentials quickly.
- Sampling strategy: deterministic reservoir sampling per credential to maintain representative traces over windows. Store 1k samples per credential/week by default (configurable).
- Heatmap resolution: for orgs with >2k credentials, aggregate into top N + "others" and allow text search to surface rows. Avoid rendering all rows at once.
- Lazy loaded sparse journeys: fetch only 3 samples when the carousel is visible; prioritize throttled samples when available.

Metrics & signals to surface (priority order):
1) throttle-events (count + rate)
2) token-cost (estimated dollars)
3) request-count
4) p50/p95 latency
5) error-rate (4xx/5xx breakdown)
6) model-variant mix (percent per model)

Edge cases / open questions:
- Multi-credential sessions: a single request can be routed via multiple credentials (e.g., proxying). How to attribute? Proposed: primary attribution to the request-level credential; secondary attribution tag for proxy chain. Need product decision.
- Quota policy changes: when a quota is changed mid-window, how to present historical throttles? Proposal: annotate timeline with policy-change markers and compute "effective quota" for intervals.
- Private deployments & PII: sampling/store policies must respect tenant preferences; default anonymize inputs for Private deployments unless customer opts-in.
- Very high-cardinality routes: some customers have 10k+ route endpoints. Provide regex/grouping rules and allow user-defined route buckets.

Wireframe notes (rough, not exhaustive):
- Desktop primary layout 3-column: (Top contributors / Heatmap / Sparse journeys). Mobile: collapse sparse journeys into a slide-up pane; heatmap becomes a stacked list with mini-sparklines.
- Color: two modes for heatmap intensity: token mode (blue->navy) and throttle mode (green->red). Provide legend and accessibility-safe palettes.
- Tooltip micro-interactions: on hover of a sparkline in top contributors show 7d delta and lightning icon if there is an associated throttle spike.

Backlog grooming output (tasks and priority):
- CORE-1 (P0): backend hourly rollups for credential x route x model (JIRA-CORE-918) -> estimate 2 sprints.
- UI-23 (P0): heatmap component + cell flyout (new reusable grid) -> 1 sprint + QA.
- UX-12 (P1): sparse journeys UI + sample carousel -> 1 sprint.
- PRIV-5 (P1): sampling policy UI for Private deployments (opt-in / anonymize) -> 1 sprint.
- ALERT-9 (P2): quick-create alert flows from row actions -> grooming.
- PERF-7 (P2): server-side pagination and top-N caching for large orgs -> grooming + infra follow-up.

Acceptance criteria (initial):
- Page loads within 1.2s for orgs with <= 200 credentials when default window = 24h.
- Clicking a heatmap cell opens flyout with metrics and at least 3 sample traces.
- Alert creation flow pre-populates threshold using selected metric and 90th-percentile baseline.

Sample copy snippets:
- Heatmap cell tooltip: "Credential: {{cred_name}} · Route: {{route}} · tokens: {{tokens_24h}} · throttled: {{throttle_pct}}%"
- Row action "Pin credential": "Pin this credential to the top of the page for quicker access across sessions."

Things to test in prototype sessions:
- Is top contributors' ranking intuitive for customers who primarily care about latency vs cost? Consider toggle mode: rank by cost / rank by throttles / rank by latency.
- Do sparse journeys help reduce mean time to triage? Measure MTTT in customer interviews.
- Sampling bias: run A/B to ensure reservoir sampling preserves rare but important throttled traces.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Sync with infra next week to validate rollup storage cost estimates (Ben).
- Quick prototype of heatmap SVG + virtualized rows in Figma + run user testing with 3 customers (Miguel).
- Draft alert templates for throttle events and token-spend anomalies (Lina).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the credential fingerprint small; users hate long ids. Maybe allow aliasing.
- Consider adding a one-click runbook link on throttle spikes pointing to a curated set of debugging steps (useful for support).
- Remember to check SRE runbooks for existing sampling legal constraints for EU customers.

Unresolved design choices (short list):
- Attribution model for proxied requests (primary vs multi-tag).
- Default sampling retention and storage cap per org (cost tradeoff).
- Whether to expose raw request payload samples in hosted product or only metadata + hashes.

End of notes.
